The Delhi Metro is the rapid transit system of Delhi and its neighbouring cities, India's largest and busiest. Its first line opened on 24 December 2002, and it now runs well over 350 km of track.

Delhi in the 1990s had choking traffic and dirty air, and an earlier metro in Kolkata had taken over twenty years to build. The Delhi Metro Rail Corporation, set up in 1995, hired E. Sreedharan, the engineer who had built the Konkan Railway. He was known for finishing work on time and for keeping politics out of contracts. Much of the money came as cheap loans from Japan.

The metro reached the satellite cities of Gurugram, Noida and Ghaziabad and changed where people live and work. It showed that India could build large urban works well, and dozens of Indian cities started metros after it. In a city whose capital was planned by the British in the 1920s, see New Delhi, it is the largest public work since.
